summary.intent: Implement PR B in a stacked PR series for the callisto repo: make the secret redactor know every secret-bearing credential name, with drift guards, using test-first development. Then begin mapping PR C (E176 cause field and PyPI status classification).
summary.outcome: PR B was completed: the redactor now knows PYPI_TOKEN and NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN, drift guards were added in the runner and provider crates, a changeset was added, and `just ci` exited 0. It was then committed and pushed. PR C was investigated but not yet started.

repo: Callisto is a multi-crate Rust workspace (callisto-model, callisto-cli, callisto-graph) worked in a stacked-PR worktree at .claude/worktrees/wave1-stack.

The secret redactor's credential name list lives in callisto-model's registry.rs, while the runner (callisto-cli) and release provider (callisto-graph) each keep their own strip lists, so these can drift apart.
Drift guard tests assert that every secret name in the runner and provider credential lists is known to the redactor, so adding a new secret to a strip list without updating the redactor fails tests.
Changesets are required in .changeset/ and `just ci` is the gate run before committing each PR.

PR C will need a `cause` field on E176 with a readable Display per cause, PyPI statuses reported as `ProviderStatus` rather than `MalformedResponse`, and updates to four registry test assertions that pin the old cause.

code.finding: Holds the redactor's credential name constant. It originally had six names and was missing PYPI_TOKEN and NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN; its doc comment was stale and was updated.
Provider drift guard test was added here, checking the provider credential list against the redactor's known names.
Runner's credential list test was extended into a drift guard against the redactor.

workflow: Test-first discipline: a compile failure is not a meaningful red, so the constant was introduced with the existing six names first so the test failed behaviorally on the missing names.
Confirm the gate's own exit line (`exit=0`) and tree state before committing rather than trusting a completion notification alone.
Avoid editing the tree while a long `just ci` gate runs in the background; use that time for read-only investigation of the next PR.
Use helper scripts in a tmp jobs directory to run multi-step test and lint commands.

friction: The sandbox rejects heredocs, so the provider test had to be appended with the Edit tool instead of a shell append.
The first test run was a compile failure, not a real red, which cost an extra iteration to restructure the constant.
open_items: PR C is not started: add the `cause` field to E176 with Display, switch PyPI response statuses to `ProviderStatus`, and update the four pinned registry test assertions.
Docs and tests that pin E176 text or PyPI causes need review when PR C is built.
PR B still needs to be stacked as a PR and its base set up before C is built on top.
